It reports 930 dead paths, which is 100 percent of the augmented track and 0 percent of the standard track, and an injected REAL dead path left the count unchanged and unnamed. MUST DO: make check 7 follow ref() transitively, as check_internal already does. Second LOB to raise a check-7 defect after Health V2, so under the promotion trigger a third raising promotes the fix or the reason it cannot be promoted goes into BUILD_RULES 12.

Coverage check 6 counts only target-track rows with outcome=mapped. On this LOB that is 442 pairs, out of a map that also carries 990 distinct augmentation satellite-and-attribute pairs, 60 of which reach no built payload. They are neither counted nor exemptible, so BUILD_RULES 8.1 -- coverage is the only check that can see silence -- does not hold over the augmentation track. Already in BUILD_RULES 12 from Health V2; this is the second LOB. MUST DO: add the augmentation container to the denominator, or state in 12 why it cannot be.

A RENUMBERING ORDINAL REACHES A CHILD KEY IN EMITTED SQL. SAT_AUG_POLICY_DOCUMENT_DISPATCH declares src_cdk DISPATCH_SERIAL_NUMBER and its stage defines it from serial_no, one of the seven ordinal spellings re-derived by shape from the source index. A dispatch line inserted or removed re-attaches the history of the rest (BUILD_RULES 5.1). Built as mapped under 5.7, correctly, with the mapper own declared-source-gap disposition, so this is a SOURCE question and not a build defect: is SERIAL_NO stable per dispatch line, and if not, what identifies one. Handback note: the build names the satellite SAT_POLICY_DOCUMENT_DISPATCH but the emitted model is SAT_AUG_POLICY_DOCUMENT_DISPATCH, and the 11 map leg rows collapse to one child-key column in one stage.

15 of the 20 collapse-trap satellite-and-leg pairs in the profile are src_cdk columns on BUILT satellites. Two satellites were refused because every leg of their child key is a no-operand literal, which was right. The rest are backed by a source column that is currently single-valued only because one view carries the leg, and the build says so. MUST DO: a mapper ruling per satellite on whether the leg really discriminates at load time. Stage 1 reports 11 here, which counts satellites whose child key is composed ONLY of trap legs -- a narrower population than the 15 leg pairs measured in the emitted models. Both are true of their own scope and the handback should say which it means.

BD12 ADJUDICATED: refusing to substitute a hub key into a link leg is the right call, and audit_mt_link_leg_divergence probes all 13 recorded divergences -- 66 left joins, 42 link-hub-feeder triples, 38 leg slots, 13 of 13 covered. Three limits must travel with it: it has never been executed, because nothing here runs dbt; orphan legs above zero is necessary but not sufficient, since a null business key dropped by the hub feed looks the same; and it cannot see a mis-bound POSITIONAL leg, because leg and hub key come from the same renderer and agree by construction. The handback should ask the mapper for the CLAIM_RESERVE ruling -- does the link attach to the FOREIGN_KEY claim or the PARENT_KEY_HASH claim -- and for the origin of the orphan EMP leg on BAGIC_RM_ECODE.
